albums.blurb: Tangerine Dream were the Berlin electronic group around Edgar Froese, and Phaedra — their fifth album and their first for the young Virgin label — was recorded at the Manor in Oxfordshire in late 1973. It marks the moment the band abandoned free-form krautrock jamming for pulsing, sequencer-driven music: the title track grew out of a Moog sequencer pattern drifting out of tune while the tape ran. Its four instrumental pieces defined what became known as the Berlin School style, ancestral to much later ambient and electronic film music.
albums.reception: Released with virtually no radio play, Phaedra reached No. 15 on the UK Albums Chart during a 15-week run and achieved six-figure sales in the UK on word of mouth alone.

albums.blurb: Ocean's second studio album proper, released in August 2016 on his own Boys Don't Cry imprint one day after the visual album Endless closed out his Def Jam contract. Where channel ORANGE leaned on full-band arrangements and character storytelling, Blonde strips the songs to sparse, often drumless sketches built on voice, guitar and keyboards, with contributors ranging from André 3000 to Jonny Greenwood; it remains his most recent studio album.
albums.reception: Blonde debuted at No. 1 on the Billboard 200 with 276,000 first-week units, the third-largest debut of 2016 behind Drake's Views and Beyoncé's Lemonade.

albums.blurb: Touré was a guitarist and farmer from Niafunké in northern Mali whose hypnotic, drone-based playing is often described as the missing link between West African music and American blues. Talking Timbuktu, recorded in three days in Los Angeles with American guitarist Ry Cooder producing and playing alongside him, was released on World Circuit in 1994 and became his international breakthrough, a decade before his celebrated late-career duet records with kora player Toumani Diabaté.
albums.reception: The album won the 1994 Grammy Award for Best World Music Album and spent 31 weeks at No. 1 on Billboard's world music chart, long ranking among the best-selling world music records.
